solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Competitive activity could yield cigar — grand!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could produce something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praises an activity for producing a splendid cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could yield' is the anagram signal: CIGAR and GRAND together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing modified cars over a short straight course is a competitive motor sport.

clue.text: It could hold sweet drops one's set to move around

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set in motion and shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is about to push drops of something around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move around' signals an anagram of DROPS and ONE'S SET. 'Sweet' is the British word for a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spoon used for eating pudding holds a portion of the sweet course.

clue.text: Boxer on street celebrity roll

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer appears on a street's list of famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places ALI above ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The top tier of famous people forms an exclusive list of stars.

clue.text: One might make catch, some hero, dashing?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are taken, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A dashing hero is imagined making a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters lifted from inside 'heRO, Dashing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's fishing pole is the tool that lands a catch of fish.

clue.text: Showcase, industrial, displaying dairy product

indicators.note: the words put on show a run of letters held within them

explanation.surface: An industrial exhibition puts a dairy product on display.
explanation.definitionFit: The main protein of milk, used to make cheese, is a product of dairy farming.

clue.text: Written comment about king made after upset in Cathedral

indicators.note: the upset word follows the first part
the comment goes around the king, enclosing him

parts.note: a note is a short written comment
R, from the Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the word made is disturbed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cathedral note mentions a king and something made after an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the famous Paris cathedral; 'after' sets the rearranged word behind the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Gothic church in Paris is a cathedral.

clue.text: Long way off about the originator

indicators.note: the distance word wraps around the second piece

parts.note: far means a long way off

explanation.surface: The originator of something is said to be a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder or creator of an idea is often called its parent, as in 'the father of modern physics'.

clue.text: Be lent geezer at work — no fast mover!

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are busy being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lend a bloke at work who is no speed merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' signals an anagram of BE LENT GEEZER. 'Geezer' is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, mild wind moves air only slowly, unlike a gale.

clue.text: Noticed spades, multi-coloured

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
pied means patched in two or more colours

explanation.surface: Someone noticed garden spades in many colours.
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught sight of something is to have noticed it.

clue.text: Supply to the full at sea, it's fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word it is taken, its apostrophe-s read as 'is' joining the fodder to the signal

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses that being fully supplied at sea is fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' signals an anagram of AT SEA and IT, with 's read as the linking 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone's appetite completely is to give them all they can want.

clue.text: Fiddling taximeter — that could lead to penalties!

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters of the word are messed about

explanation.surface: A cab driver's rigged meter could get them fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddling' is the anagram signal. 'Penalties' here means a football penalty shoot-out, which follows the added period in a drawn knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a drawn cup tie goes to an added period and then possibly to a penalty shoot-out.

clue.text: A loan peer arranged, one moving up?

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A lord arranges a loan, hoping to rise in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals an anagram of A LOAN PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft climbs into the sky, so it is literally something moving upward.

clue.text: Baking stolen

definitions.meaning: baking means extremely warm, as in a baking day
slang for stolen goods that are risky to handle

explanation.surface: Something being baked turns out to be stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both very warm and, in slang, recently stolen.

clue.text: Mike leaving wood finds river

indicators.note: Mike departs, so his letter goes out of the wood

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike leaves the woods and comes across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is the radio code word for M.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Rome is a well-known example of a river.

clue.text: In poem bishop replaces second hat

indicators.note: the bishop takes the place of the second's letter in the poem

parts.note: a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: In a poem, a bishop swaps something for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimless cap tied under the chin is a type of headwear.

clue.text: Have same opinion: an excessive desire must be cut

indicators.note: the word for desire is docked of its last letter

explanation.surface: Everyone concurs that excessive desire must be curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be cut' trims the last letter from GREED.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur with someone is to share their view.

clue.text: German author's attempt overlooks English theory, half completed

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the German author

indicators.note: in a down clue the attempt sits above the following letters
only the first half of the word is done, so its opening letters are taken

explanation.surface: A German writer attempts to ignore English theory, only half finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half completed' keeps the first three of six letters of THEORY.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Faust is Germany's most celebrated writer.

clue.text: Criticise sleep on return

indicators.note: the word for sleep comes back, reading in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for sleeping when they get back.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewers slate or slam a poor show, which is to criticise it harshly.

clue.text: Principal lecturer's claim disheartened Oscar

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the principal lecturer

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outer letters of the name remain

explanation.surface: A senior academic's claim left Oscar dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle of OSCAR, leaving OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior academic rank in a university department is the chair holder.

clue.text: Reject with contempt ultimately useless banal stuff

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: corn is trite or sentimental material

explanation.surface: Someone rejects worthless, banal material with disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn or disdain something is to dismiss it contemptuously.

clue.text: Plain about account for ham

indicators.note: the plain word goes around the account abbreviation

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view

explanation.surface: A plain statement about how a ham was accounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like meat but is a verb here: to perform in an exaggerated way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammy actor exaggerates, so to ham it up is to overdo a performance.

clue.text: Gave talk, producing part of wheel

definitions.meaning: past tense of speak, meaning delivered a talk
a rod joining the hub of a wheel to its rim

explanation.surface: A speaker produced a component of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of speak and a radial bar in a wheel.

clue.text: Title seems ideal, respectful first of all

indicators.note: the opening letter of every one of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: A title seems the ideal form of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' takes the initials of SEEMS, IDEAL, RESPECTFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorific of a knight is a form of address and rank.

clue.text: Revised rent decree that puts people off?

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new decree on rents is meant to discourage people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' signals an anagram of RENT DECREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement by threat of consequences is what keeps people from acting.
